## Natural history notes

A large paper wasp characterized by a mostly reddish-brown body, smoky wings, long dangling legs in flight, and fine sculpturing on the back of the thorax. In Florida, the Fine-backed Red Paper Wasp is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, gardens, parks, yards, sheds, eaves, and other sheltered places where it can attach open paper nests. Adults visit flowers and sugary resources, while females hunt caterpillars and other soft-bodied insects to feed the larvae; colonies can sting defensively if the nest is disturbed, so nests should be observed from a distance.
